dog.description_text: Meet Micro — New Arrival! Micro just arrived and is still getting settled in, so we’re just beginning to learn who they are. Right now, everything is new—new people, new sounds, new routines—and we’re giving them time to relax, decompress, and show us their true personality at their own pace. Here’s what we know so far about his time in foster care: https://bestfriends.sharepoint.com/:b:/r/sites/GRP_NYC_Foster/Shared%20Documents/Forms/AllItems.aspx?id=%2Fsites%2FGRP%5FNYC%5FFoster%2FShared%20Documents%2FGeneral%2FMicro%20%2D%20About%20Me%2Epdf&parent=%2Fsites%2FGRP%5FNYC%5FFoster%2FShared%20Documents%2FGeneral&p=true&share=cQq8aP8erUMHRoALo83gVOm9EgUC5IdCAKdMblQRvA%5FkI4wRmg Micro is missing an eye but it doesnt slow his down in the slightest. He is very playful and affectionate. His foster says "Micro was put on this earth to seek love from other people. Naturally, he acclimatises to his environment very quickly, as long as there is a person there to help lovingly guide him through his big emotions. When we brought Micro home, he immediately sought out cuddles from us, within 48 hours he would explore our house and return to under the bed to sleep - but would always seek out snuggles where he could and would follow us around the house. At one week, Micro was fully acclimatised to his environment and comfortable with his situation. I love Micro, because Micro wants to be loved so much and has so much love to give. He will follow us around the house, and constantly seek out snuggles and affection. All he wants is to feel included and does not have a single mean bone in whole body. Micro loves cat TV, we put on for him for his entertainment and he is mesmerised by the pretty colours of fake fish tanks and will spend hours watching it and trying to eat the fishies.". He is a lap cat and a total joy. He has been neutered, vaccinated, microchipped, and has had preventative treatments to ensure he is ready for his next steps. Submit an adoption survey from above and our team will reach out via phone or email (check spam) to schedule a counseling call. Please remember, pets cannot be held or reserved.
